scheme_name: Creation of Modern Facilities in Market Committee: Scheme to provide assistance foe setting up modern facilities in Market Committee
description:
The "Creation of Modern Facilities in Market Committee" scheme was launched by the Government of India in the year 2018. 

This initiative aims to enhance the infrastructure of agricultural markets across the country. 

The scheme is designed to provide financial assistance to State Agricultural Marketing Boards. 

The objective is to modernize existing agricultural market committees. 

The government seeks to create a more efficient and effective marketing system for agricultural produce. 

The scheme focuses on improving the quality of market infrastructure. 

This includes the establishment of modern facilities such as cold storage, warehouses, and grading units. 

The target is to set up these facilities in various agricultural markets across India. 

The scheme aims to benefit farmers by providing them with better access to markets. 

It also aims to reduce post-harvest losses which can be as high as 20 to 30 percent in some crops. 

The expected outcome is to increase the farmers' income by ensuring better prices for their produce. 

The scheme allocates a budget of ₹200 crore for its implementation. 

This amount is to be utilized for the development of modern facilities in various market committees. 

The financial assistance provided under this scheme can cover up to 50 percent of the project cost. 

For projects in the northeastern states and hilly regions, the assistance can go up to 75 percent. 

The minimum project cost eligible for assistance is set at ₹10 lakh. 

The maximum limit for assistance is capped at ₹1 crore per project. 

Eligibility for this scheme is primarily focused on State Agricultural Marketing Boards. 

These boards must be registered under the Agricultural Produce Market Committee Act. 

They should also have a clear plan for the development of market infrastructure. 

The application process involves submitting a detailed project proposal. 

This proposal must outline the objectives, expected outcomes, and financial requirements. 

The proposal should also include a timeline for project completion. 

Required documents include proof of registration of the marketing board. 

Additionally, a detailed project report must be submitted. 

This report should include technical specifications and cost estimates. 

The application must be submitted to the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

Once the proposal is received, it will be evaluated by a technical committee. 

The committee will assess the feasibility and viability of the project. 

If approved, the financial assistance will be disbursed in installments. 

The first installment is typically released upon project approval. 

Subsequent installments are released based on the progress of the project. 

The timeline for project completion is generally set at 18 months from the date of approval. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

The ministry collaborates with various state governments to ensure effective implementation. 

Regular monitoring and evaluation are conducted to assess the impact of the scheme. 

The scheme also aims to promote the use of technology in agricultural marketing. 

This includes the establishment of e-marketing platforms for better price discovery. 

Farmers will be trained on how to use these platforms effectively. 

The scheme is expected to create a more competitive market environment. 

This will ultimately benefit the consumers as well by providing better quality produce. 

The government aims to enhance the overall agricultural supply chain through this initiative. 

It is also aligned with the broader goals of the National Agricultural Policy. 

The policy emphasizes the need for modernizing agriculture and improving farmers' livelihoods. 

The scheme is part of the larger effort to double farmers' income by the year 2022. 

The government has set a target to modernize at least 1,000 agricultural markets under this scheme. 

As of October 2023, progress reports indicate that several states have initiated projects. 

States like Punjab, Haryana, and Maharashtra are leading in project implementation. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from farmers and agricultural experts. 

They have noted improvements in market access and reduced wastage of produce. 

The government is committed to ensuring transparency in the disbursement of funds. 

Regular audits are conducted to ensure that the funds are utilized effectively. 

The scheme is expected to contribute significantly to the agricultural sector's growth. 

It aims to create a sustainable and resilient agricultural economy in India. 

Farmers are encouraged to actively participate in the development of their local markets. 

This will empower them and enhance their bargaining power in the market. 

The scheme is a step towards achieving food security and improving rural livelihoods. 

The government continues to promote awareness about the scheme among stakeholders. 

Workshops and seminars are organized to educate farmers about the benefits. 

The scheme is also linked with other government initiatives for holistic development. 

This includes the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi and the PM Fasal Bima Yojana. 

Overall, the "Creation of Modern Facilities in Market Committee" scheme represents a significant investment in the agricultural infrastructure of India. 

It aims to create a more robust and efficient agricultural marketing system. 

This will ultimately lead to improved economic conditions for farmers across the nation. 

The government remains committed to monitoring the progress of this scheme closely. 

Future expansions and modifications to the scheme will be based on feedback and outcomes observed. 

The focus remains on creating a sustainable agricultural ecosystem that benefits all stakeholders involved.
